content: The FNTA protein, also known as farnesyltransferase/geranylgeranyltransferase type-1 subunit alpha, is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the FNTA gene. Prenyltransferases are enzymes that catalyze the attachment of either a farnesyl group or a geranylgeranyl group to the cysteine residue of proteins that contain a C-terminal CAAX box. This attachment occurs via a thioether linkage. CAAX geranylgeranyltransferase and CAAX farnesyltransferase are heterodimeric enzymes. They share the same alpha subunit but differ in their beta subunits. The FNTA gene specifically encodes the alpha subunit of these transferases. Through alternative splicing, the FNTA gene produces multiple transcript variants, which encode different isoforms of the protein. In terms of protein interactions, FNTA has been demonstrated to interact with the TGF-beta receptor 1.
